doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: Young musicians and the end of the jazz apprenticeship
summary: The apprenticeship system has largely been replaced by mentorship through schools, though sessions and clubs still exist.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I think you mentioned something I read that the current generation of aspiring young jazz artists not only have to be good improvisers with their instruments, they have to improvise their career. How do we make up for the fact that the jam sessions and the small club gigs and the touring bands are mostly a thing of the past?

Well I wouldn’t say that the small club gigs, I mean there are still sessions, I mean my students here in New York, well prior to the pandemic of course, but there are still these clubs like Small’s in New York where students get together and do their little gigs and play. And there are still plenty of sessions. I mean a lot of it is now through the veneer of education I guess. I mean it used to be the jazz apprenticeship system for decades and © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

decades was a really important thing where you had, you know, great established musicians who would hire young guys, and now young women we can say, to play with them and give them seasoning. But now that the jazz apprenticeship system is almost entirely defunct a lot of it now is mentorship that’s done through the schools. I know I’ve taken some students kind of under my wing and done stuff with them and for them, and I know lots of my colleagues have done the same thing. So now it’s done through the schools. But it’s still done. I mean there’s X amount of work that’s got to be done, there’s X amount of experience that these kids have to have somehow or other because I mean very few people, you know, when they’re very young are totally mature and seasoned. I mean that’s extremely rare. They’ve got to get experience and chops and maturity through whatever means possible and so however you do it you’ve got to do it.
